findings.title: A config read failure in one worktree aborts the whole worktree loop
findings.description:
`installCheckout` awaits `readRulesExclude(root)` before calling `installIde`. That calls `ConfigManager.get`, which rethrows any non-ENOENT error from `readToml` (`packages/core/src/config/ConfigManager.ts:21-31`), such as a malformed TOML file. It also throws a plain `Error` if the value is not a string.

The `installWorktrees` doc comment says "any other exception is a bug and propagates". A broken `.toml` in one worktree is a user-environment error, not a bug. It escapes the loop, so the remaining worktrees are never installed. `installCommandsForTarget` is also skipped. The user gets only a generic `handleError` message with no worktree name.

This conflicts with the loop's stated contract that "a failing worktree does not stop the others". Catch config-read failures inside `installCheckout`, or inside the loop. Name the worktree, record it in `failed`, and continue.

No test covers this path. The new worktree tests only exercise `installIde` returning exit 1 and `installIde` throwing.

findings.title: Dry run hard-codes the set of paths a target can write
findings.description:
`INSTALL_PATHS` repeats `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude`, `.cursor`, `.github` and `.agents` as bare literals. These are the same paths already described by `TARGETS[...].markerFiles` and by `AGENT_SKILLS_DIR` in `ideTargets.ts`.

The old `propagateDirs` descriptor field was removed. As a result, the "which paths does a target write" knowledge now lives in two unconnected places. The project rules say a value should be defined once, so that changing it means editing one place.

If a target starts writing a new top-level path, the sandbox will not copy it. The dry-run report will then show it as added when it already exists, or miss modifications to it. Nothing fails or warns when that happens. Derive the list from a per-target descriptor, or add a test that every path an install writes is covered by `INSTALL_PATHS`.

findings.title: Positional parameter lists on the new helpers
findings.description: `installCheckout(guideDir, root, target, flags)` and `installWorktrees(project, guideDir, target, flags)` take four positional arguments. The TypeScript rules prefer a destructured options object for three or more. `guideDir` and `root` are both plain strings, so swapping them would compile without error. Low risk, but cheap to fix.

findings.title: Stray formatting and a stale header comment
findings.description: There is a leftover double blank line before `describe('cf setup-ide', ...)`. Separately, the `ideTargets.ts` header comment (lines 5-7) still frames the module around `worktreePropagation` acyclicity. That module no longer imports it.

findings.title: Test coverage and structure for the new installer
findings.description:
The new tests cover the main paths:
- Dry run: fresh, no-changes and guide-changed cases, plus sandbox cleanup when the install aborts.
- Lint: check and write behaviour, including the C# depth boundary.
- `rules.exclude`: patterns, prune and warnings.
- `missingRequirements` edge cases.
- A real-guide smoke test.

Tests live in `tests/`, follow the `{module}.test.ts` naming and use Vitest. The installer is mocked at the `installIde` boundary in `setup-ide.test.ts`, which avoids duplicating its behaviour tests. The `describe.each` over the four targets for the overwrite prompt is compact and checks behaviour.
